chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and do righteous deeds.
Except for what they accept from his whispers.
ai.seo_question: What is the extent of Satan's authority over believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that Satan's dominion is not coercive but contingent upon the believer's internal acceptance of his whispers, distinguishing between mere suggestion and genuine influence. This hadith underscores the Shia theological principle of human free will (*ikhtiyar*), affirming that spiritual victory is achieved through conscious vigilance (*muraqabah*) against the self and the devil. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the mechanics of temptation, where the devil acts as a persistent caller rather than an absolute ruler.
